Subject: Pin routing decision paths for Aurelia Health

Hi Liam / Aurelia Security team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear set of requirements. Quick post-call recap and a few clarifying questions so we can line up the technical deep-dive and proposal: 

Summary from call:
- Primary requirement: Patient records (PII) must remain in the EU for residency/compliance.
- Logs and ephemeral debugging traces preferred to remain in-region but Aurelia can accept copies for diagnostic purposes in the US if strictly limited and encrypted.
- Desired RPO/RTO: you mentioned RPO in the 1–4 hour range and RTO targeted under 2 hours for critical flows.
- Key question: can Redwood provide a warm-standby cross-region failover that keeps primary data pinned to EU while allowing backups to land in US only for DR?

Clarifying questions for your team (so Ben can prepare the deep-dive):
1) Which categories of data do you classify as non-negotiable EU-only? (e.g., PHI/patient records vs. diagnostic logs)
2) Do you require customer-managed keys (CMK) for data at rest, or would a Redwood-managed KMS with strict access controls be acceptable for hosted?
3) Audit log retention target — you mentioned multi-year retention; can you confirm the minimum (e.g., 7 years vs. 3 years)?
4) Are there any regulatory constraints on cross-border backups even if encrypted and strictly for DR?

Next steps I propose:
- Ben will draft a short options matrix (pinning + failover trade-offs) and a recommended configuration for a hosted vs. dedicated deployment.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your security and infra SMEs (Ben + Grace + our infra engineer).
- Share the SOC2 report and sample data flow diagram.

I've attached a short post-call summary and the calendar invite options in the Drive link below. If you can answer the clarifying Qs inline, that will help us tailor the deep-dive.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pin routing decision paths for Aurelia Health

Tessa, thanks — quick answers from our side below.

1) EU-only: patient records (PHI), user profiles tied to patient identifiers, and any consent metadata.
2) CMK: preferred for PHI; if Redwood supports a KMS integration where keys are controlled by Aurelia (bring-your-own-key) that meets our key rotation/audit needs, that would be ideal. For logs we can accept platform-managed keys.
3) Audit logs: regulatory team asks for 7 years for certain events (access, export, consent changes), but we can start with an initial 3-year retention for non-critical events if needed while we evaluate cost.
4) Cross-border backups: allowed only for encrypted, access-restricted backups used strictly for disaster recovery. They cannot be used for analytics or training.

Also: can you confirm whether full snapshots include KV caches and prompt context, or if those are excluded from cross-region backups? That affects our classification of what can leave the EU.

Happy to schedule the deep-dive — availability next week is Tue/Wed mornings CET.

Liam O'Connell

Hi Liam — scope and constraints noted. Below is a technical summary and recommended configuration for your EU-PHI requirement plus warm-standby DR in the US.

High-level options (attached matrix: redwood_pin_options.xlsx):
- Option A (Recommended): Primary EU pinning (customer traffic, storage, and KV caches hosted in EU). Asynchronous disaster backups (snapshots) replicated to US cold/warm bucket with CMK support. Backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys where available (see KMS notes). Cross-region copies are tagged as DR-only and access-controlled; not used for analytics or training.
- Option B: Dedicated EU-only deployment (on-prem or VPC) for PHI with no cross-border backups; logs exported to your SIEM in the US via encrypted forwarders. Higher cost, lower flexibility.

Technical clarifications:*
- Snapshots and KV cache: Snapshots include persistent model state and storage artifacts but not in-memory ephemeral KV caches; we persist a sanitized checkpoint for restore, which excludes transient prompt context unless explicitly configured.
- KMS/CMK: Hosted supports customer-managed keys through our enterprise KMS integrations (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS). For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) you can bring an HSM-backed key and we can configure encryption-at-rest using your key via our key wrapping flow. See kms_integration_notes.txt attached.
- Logging & audit: Audit events can be retained for 90 days by default (configurable). For enterprise customers we support extended retention up to multi-year with tiered storage and export hooks to your S3/GCS archive or to your SIEM via syslog. Sensitive audit events (access/export) can be retained per your 7-year requirement with proper archival.
- Access controls: Fine-grained RBAC + token-level redaction for logs. We also support disabling token-level logging for specific routes/services on a per-tenant basis.
- Failover behavior: Warm-standby in US is supported as an async DR path. Automatic failover is configurable but we recommend a manual cutover for PHI flows to ensure compliance sign-off. RTO/RPO estimates depend on workload — for small-batch request load we can meet <2 hour RTO with snapshot+warm nodes; for high-throughput real-time flows we recommend Dedicated with pre-warmed capacity.

Attachments: redwood_pin_options.xlsx (tradeoff matrix), kms_integration_notes.txt (integration details).

Suggested next steps:
1) Confirm the list of EU-only data classes (Liam email below).
2) Book the technical deep-dive — propose Tue 2026-12-08 at 10:00 CET (60m) with your infra/security and our infra lead.
3) We'll include a short mutual action plan after the deep-dive and produce a configuration-level diagram for legal review.
